sections.h2: How does Miami Beach's history shape a house sale today?
sections.html:
The city began as a barrier island joined to the mainland by the Collins Bridge, and it incorporated on March 26, 1915. Hotels, shopping streets and residential neighborhoods followed within a few decades, which is why a Miami Beach street can mix very different buildings.

The city's economic development writeup lists hospitality, retail, technology, healthcare, finance and the arts among its key sectors, and its rental and zoning rules are strict, as the rental section below shows.

  • Pricing: compare your house with sales of the same building type, not the whole city.
  • Rental rules: confirm what a buyer may legally do with the property.
  • Records: collect permits, association documents and insurance history.

sections.h2: What does QuickFacts say about housing and residents here?
sections.html:
Miami Beach has 7.69 square miles of land. Federal estimates for mid-2025 show 81,594 people, compared with 82,890 counted in 2020 and 87,779 in 2010, a slow slide over fifteen years.

The survey period 2020 to 2024 found 41,600 households averaging 1.95 people, and 18.8 percent of residents are 65 or older. About four in five residents (81.4 percent) had not moved in the previous year. Households this small and this settled often sell because of an estate or a move to smaller quarters, and each of those has its own paperwork.

sections.h2: Can I use my Miami Beach house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Not a single-family house. The Resiliency Code, in sections 7.5.4.13(d)(E) and 7.5.4.11(a), bars rentals of less than six months and one day in all single-family homes and in many multi-family buildings in certain zoning districts.

Rentals that are allowed need a city Business Tax Receipt and a Resort Tax account. City code section 102-386 requires both numbers in every advertisement or listing. The city also publishes a list of apartment buildings authorized for short-term rental, grouped by zoning district.

A buyer who plans nightly stays will check these rules, and so should you. If your past income came from stays the code forbids, expect offers to be priced as a long-term rental or an owner-occupied home. Code Compliance and the city's Customer Service Center take reports of illegal rentals, and the city publishes a zoning map to check a property.

sections.h2: What does a Miami Beach seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade is the one Florida county with its own deed stamp structure: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not apply to a deed transferring only a single-family dwelling. Every other county charges 70 cents.

The base is the price plus any mortgage or lien on the property, whether the buyer assumes it or not. The clerk of court takes payment at the moment the deed is recorded.

  • Payoff letters for the mortgage, any home equity line and judgment liens.
  • Unpaid property tax for the year, prorated with the buyer.
  • For condos and co-ops, an estoppel or payoff letter from the association.
  • Title insurance and recording, as set out in the contract.

sections.h2: How do Miami-Dade property tax dates affect a Miami Beach sale?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade's property appraiser sets assessments, and the county's tax collector sends the bills. The appraiser's office says it does not send bills and does not set or collect taxes. It certified the 2026 roll on October 16, 2026.

Florida bills arrive in November. The early-payment discount starts at 4 percent in November and drops a point each month through February. An unpaid bill turns delinquent after April 1.

Selling a homestead ends the exemption on that parcel, and the new owner is assessed at full market-based value from the next New Year's Day. A seller moving within Florida may carry over the saved amount by filing for portability along with the new homestead application by March 1.

sections.h2: What if the Miami Beach house is inherited or tenant-occupied?
sections.html:
No heir can deed the house until a court gives someone authority. Florida's short-form summary administration is open to small estates, up to $150,000 outside exempt property, and to deaths from over two years back.

A tenant complicates timing. A landlord can serve a 3-day written demand for unpaid rent, not counting weekends or court holidays, and a monthly tenancy ends on 30 days' notice. If the tenant stays past a court judgment, the sheriff posts a 24-hour notice before restoring possession.

Many buyers prefer a vacant house, so decide early whether you will deliver it empty or sell it with the lease in place.

sections.h2: What if the mortgage is past due?
sections.html:
Get the payoff amount and the court case status from your lender in writing. Once final judgment is entered, the clerk sets the sale roughly three to five weeks out, and the lender can agree to a later date.

A sale that pays the lender off before that date protects any equity you hold. After a foreclosure sale, the clerk is the contact for surplus funds.

sections.h2: Which Miami Beach records should I gather before listing?
sections.html:
Pull together the deed, your newest tax bill, any association documents and the insurance declarations page. Add permits for roofs, windows, air conditioning and electrical work, since buyers and their lenders tend to ask.

If the property has ever been rented short term, collect the Business Tax Receipt and Resort Tax paperwork. If it was never approved, say so plainly to buyers instead of letting an inspector or the city raise it first.

The county clerk runs a free property fraud alert that emails an owner within 24 hours when a deed or mortgage is filed under their name. It takes a few minutes to join.

sections.h2: How do I weigh a cash offer against listing here?
sections.html:
Subtract commission, repairs and holding costs from a realistic list price, then set the result next to the written cash figure. The offer should name who covers the stamp tax, the title policy and recording, and say what happens to a deposit.

Ask for the settlement date and the closing agent in writing. If the buyer wants to assign the contract to someone else, ask who that person is before you commit.

faqs.q: When did Miami Beach become a city?
faqs.a: A city history article gives March 26, 1915 as the incorporation date, when the area was an undeveloped barrier island linked to the mainland by the Collins Bridge.

faqs.q: Is short-term renting allowed in Miami Beach houses?
faqs.a: No for single-family homes. The city prohibits rentals of less than six months and one day there, and allows them only in certain multi-family buildings and zoning districts with a Business Tax Receipt and Resort Tax account.
The Census Bureau lists 7.69 square miles of land, with 10,774.7 people per square mile in 2020.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax in Miami Beach the same as in other counties?
faqs.a: No. Miami-Dade charges its own combination of 60 cents and a 45 cent surtax per hundred dollars, and a single-family deed skips the surtax; the rest of the state uses 70 cents.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my reduced homestead assessment?
faqs.a: No. The new owner starts at full assessed value after the next January 1. You may be able to take your saved amount to a new Florida homestead.
